principles.p1_text: We're all Philadelphians solving a problem together.
principles.p2_title: The problem is in the system, not individuals.
principles.p2_text: No blame, no shame. The system was designed for a different economy.
principles.p3_text: Shepherds focus on solutions with love. Be the shepherd when advocating for LIFT. In the room with us? Share your fear, uncertainty, and doubt—we'll help you through it.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.intro: For 10 years, Philadelphia's smallest businesses had a shield from BIRT (Business Income and Receipts Tax)—letting them start, grow, and support their families.

impact_card.condition: If in 2025 you earned $50,000 and you are a:
impact_card.result_title: Starting in April 2026, your Philadelphia tax bill will increase by:
impact_card.conclusion: That's between 1 and 3 months' rent for many Philadelphians who simply can't afford it.

problem.stat_description: That includes 75,000 Philadelphians who own and operate single-owner entities: contractors, freelancers, gig workers, nurses, barbers, food truck vendors, artists, retailers, and more.

solution.title: The Solution: The LIFT Act
solution.intro: Pioneering legislation introduced in November 2025 by Councilman Mike Driscoll, the LIFT Act fixes the system instead of patching it by acknowledging a tax class that already exists but is unrecognized by current BIRT law.
solution.class_description: This class includes Laborers (Independent Contractors), and any individual or family enterprises with an individual owner (including those with employees).
solution.uniformity_clause: Meets PA Constitution's Uniformity Clause requirements. Confirmed by Philadelphia Law Dept.
enables: City Council and the Mayor can legally remove BIRT for the LIFT class* completely
NPT tax remains, ensuring fair taxation instead of the current double-taxation structure
Keeps money in local neighborhoods—every dollar retained turns into $3+ in local spending
solution.result: Result for an individual or family earning $50K: completely eliminates the surprise tax increase
solution.lift_class_note: *LIFT class includes Laborers (Independent Contractors), and any individual or family enterprises with an individual owner (including those with employees).

action1.title: Calculate Your Increase Before Filing
action1.description: Use the calculator at liftphilly.org/calculator to see your tax increase, then share it with your professional network so they can calculate theirs.

action2.title: Start Conversations
action2.prompt: "If you had to pay 1-3 months extra rent in taxes in 2026 and beyond, how would that affect your ability to care for yourself, your family, and your community?"
action2.followup: Then listen. Report back what you hear.

action3.title: Help Us Reach the Whole City
action3.p1: Share this information with your friends & trusted community leaders, and help us grow our network of networks.
action3.p2: Know someone who can help spread the word through your community, share their experiences as a small business owner, or both? We're looking for both formal leaders and informal connectors.

action4.title: Identify Testimony Voices
action4.intro: We're building a coalition that reflects all of Philadelphia—every zip code, every background, every identity. Help us find powerful voices from:
action4.categories_suffix: and your industry or category, too!

footer.cta: Take this sheet. Try the conversation. Calculate your impact. Join the coalition.
